correctness.rationale: The complete 2x2 Q=I-R^TR minor computation is algebraically verified (Q22, Q12, det Q). g_t is strictly increasing since g_t prime=3(tx-2/3)^2+8/3. Signs at x=2/t and 4/(1+t) plus Q22 >=0 give the exact single interval for each t, including t=1 endpoint R=-I. Implicit differentiation gives the unique t=3/8 maximizer 8/3. Eigenvalue analysis yields the precise real-root and complex-root spectral intervals; comparison of their polynomials proves S>E outside t=1 and S/E~2^(-1/3)t^(1/3). The standalone verify.py passed exact polynomial checks; analytical argument, not numerical sampling, proves universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Primary arXiv:2308.05689v1 gives local structural criteria for semidissipative RK stability, but not a closed exact full-step phase diagram in the oscillator coupling, its unique optimum t=3/8, or the spectral-versus-energy divergence. A prior fixed t=1 calculation is explicitly excluded from novelty. arXiv:2310.19758v1 similarly gives local conditions; arXiv:2201.06501 provides general energy estimates, not this optimization. Related split-step damped-oscillator and variable RK-order computations were compared by implications and do not subsume the new parametric optimization. Exact equivalence cannot be ruled out in unindexed literature.

value.rationale: A semidissipative hypocoercive ODE is physically energy-contracting, but the same explicit RK2 method admits a sharp nontrivial frequency-dependent energy-safe step. A unique optimal normalized skew-to-damping coupling at 3/8 permits the largest step 8/3; for stiff oscillatory coupling the eigenvalue-based RK allowance exceeds the physically energy-safe one by an arbitrarily large factor. These are structurally motivated and nontrivial numerical-stability design facts; a previously known single-ratio threshold cannot supply the family optimum or diverging spectral-energy gap.
